Metrics collection and the metrics store

The Collection page lists every scrape target (device × collector) that feeds SATOM's local time-series store, with its own interval, on/off switch and last outcome — the place where collection frequency is changed.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view operations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereAdministrator → Collection (every ADOM; operators: Monitoring → Collection) (URL /monitoring/collection/)

What is it?#

SATOM keeps device telemetry — CPU, memory, sessions, per-policy load, interface counters, licence headroom, log-collector state — in a local time-series store (VictoriaMetrics, single node). It fills that store by running scrape targets: one row per (device, collector). A collector makes one call to the device and turns the answer into many series, so a FortiWeb with hundreds of server policies still costs one call for its policies collector.

The Collection page is where you see every target, change how often it runs, switch it off, and check whether the store is up.

What does it do?#

  • Lists every scrape target visible in the current ADOM: Device, Collector, Interval (min), Enabled, Last run (UTC), Status (ok, error, never), Series written by the last run and duration (ms).
  • Shows the store status card Metrics store (VictoriaMetrics, this node): up/DOWN, endpoint (loopback only), total series, and the retention note Raw retention 396 days at full resolution — no rollup averaging. Under it, the Peer dual-write line says whether this node's samples are also written to the HA peer (see Advanced).
  • Shows the Store snapshots and nodes card: the store state of each node (state, series, last write) and the list of existing store snapshots, with Take snapshot and Delete for users who can change configuration.
  • Lets you edit each target's interval and, for the two expensive collectors, its top N.
  • Run sweep now runs every due target immediately.
  • Lists devices that produce no targets, with the reason (see Troubleshooting).

Requirements#

  • The metrics store service (satom-metrics) installed and running on this node. The installer places it; see Services and timers.
  • For scheduled collection: the metrics_scrape scheduled action (Fleet metrics — scrape to the local store), every 3 minutes. It is part of the standard seed plan but is not created on a fresh install until you run sudo satom execute seed actions --yes or create it in Scheduled actions.
  • Appliances registered with a reachable host and not in maintenance.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

  • Viewing the page: the legacy view gate — any read permission, for example monitoring.view; all system profiles have it.
  • Editing a target, Enable/Disable, Run sweep now, Take snapshot and Delete snapshot: the legacy config_write gate — any profile containing, for example, operations.apply or appliances.apply (full list in Monitoring overview). Without it these buttons and the interval fields are not rendered (the page is read-only) and the endpoints answer 403.
  • The sidebar entry sits in the Administrator group for users with users.manage (Administrator). Users who hold config_write but not users.manage (for example Operator) find Collection at the end of the Monitoring submenu instead.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: viewing the Collection page requires a read permission; operators find it in the Monitoring menu; the edit controls are shown only to users who can use them; and the page shows peer dual-write status and store snapshots.

How to use#

Change how often a target runs#

  1. Open Administrator → Collection (operators: Monitoring → Collection).
  2. In the target's row, type a new value in Interval (min) (1–1440). For traffic and transactions, you can also change top (1–200).
  3. Click the check-mark button at the end of the row (save interval / top-N).
  4. A flash confirms, e.g. Target fweb-01/policies: interval=5.

Stop or resume a target#

Click Disable (or Enable) in the Enabled column. The badge switches between on and off.

Collect now#

Click Run sweep now (top right). The sweep runs inside your request and reports Scrape sweep: N/M ok, E error(s), S series in T ms. Only targets that are due run — a target whose interval has not elapsed is skipped.

Take or delete a store snapshot#

  1. In the Store snapshots and nodes card, click Take snapshot. A flash names the new snapshot (Snapshot <name>).
  2. To remove one, click Delete next to it in the Snapshots list and confirm.

Snapshots never expire on their own, so delete the ones you no longer need.

Configuration#

Collectors#

Collector (label on the page) Products Default interval Call cost
box — Box resources (CPU, memory, sessions) FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator 3 min 1 per device
capacity — Licence headroom & FortiToken pools FortiAuthenticator 3 min 1 per device
policies — Server policies: sessions / conn rate / RTT FortiWeb 3 min 1 per device
interfaces — Interfaces: link state + byte counters FortiWeb, FortiADC 3 min 1 per device
vservers — Virtual servers: sessions / RTT / pool health FortiADC 3 min 1 per device
traffic — Throughput: device total + top-N policies FortiWeb 15 min (top 10) 1 per policy
transactions — HTTP transactions, top-N policies FortiWeb 60 min (top 10) 1 per policy
identity — Identity inventory: accounts, groups, tokens, certs, clients FortiAuthenticator 15 min several
faz — Log collector: volume, storage, alerts, incidents, devices, tasks FortiAnalyzer 15 min several
http_status — HTTP response classes counted from the traffic log FortiWeb 5 min 1 per policy
infra — the VM and its hypervisor host: CPU, memory, disk, network, load FortiWeb, FortiADC — only when mapped 3 min 1 per device
snmp — SNMP v2c: uptime, interfaces with 64-bit counters, CPU / memory / disk from the vendor MIB every product — only when SNMP is enabled on the appliance's form (3.4.0) 3 min a few UDP requests per device

Changed on 2026-10-14. infra reads the hypervisor, not the appliance, so it needs the device mapped to its VM (hypervisor, VM id and node in the Sentinel topology map) and a registered hypervisor. Its target is created only once that mapping is complete, on the next sweep after it is saved. Before this change every FortiWeb and FortiADC got an infra target that failed every 3 minutes until it was mapped, and a hardware appliance can never be mapped.

The two per-policy collectors only read the top N policies ranked by live connection rate; traffic always adds the device total.

Beyond the device APIs: SNMP and syslog (3.4.0)#

Every collector above reads the appliance's own REST or CLI. Two paths read what the box says over standard protocols instead — the Network Automation Forum's framework asks a Collector for exactly this (see Where SATOM sits in the NAF Framework).

SNMP polling is opt-in per appliance. On the appliance's edit form switch SNMP on, keep the port at 161 unless the box listens elsewhere and enter the community: it is stored like the passwords, in the vault when one is configured, and never shown again (an enabled switch without a community is refused when you save). Switching it off disables the snmp target rather than leaving a red row. On the appliance itself SNMP v2c must be enabled with that community, the management interface must allow SNMP, and both SATOM nodes of a pair must be listed as query hosts. The collector reads sysUpTime, the interface table (ifDescr, operational status, the 64-bit byte counters when the box serves them) and CPU, memory and disk from the vendor MIB — verified on FortiWeb 7.6.8; for the other products the documented OIDs are used with HOST-RESOURCES as the fallback, and the series say so. A box that does not answer writes satom_scrape_up{collector="snmp"} 0, never silence.

The syslog receiver runs inside the scheduler sidecar on the primary only (never on a standby) and is off by default. Its card on this page shows its state, the senders it heard from with counts per severity and facility, what it dropped and why, and — in the Global ADOM only — the last 500 lines with credential-shaped values blanked. Its settings are on the same card: bind address and port (default 0.0.0.0:5514), TCP in addition to UDP, and extra sender networks. It accepts RFC 3164, RFC 5424 and the Fortinet key=value body, over UDP or TCP with octet-counting or newline framing, and keeps only what a known sender says — the management addresses of the registered appliances plus the extra networks; anything else is dropped and counted in satom_syslog_dropped_total{reason}. Series: satom_syslog_messages_total{device,facility,severity} and satom_syslog_up{device}.

ℹ️Note — Port 514

The receiver binds an unprivileged port on purpose. Sending to 514 needs a port redirect on the node, or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE on the scheduler's unit — a change to the installed unit files, which only a signed release carries.

💡Tip — FortiWeb only sends after its syslog daemon is toggled

On a FortiWeb, after changing the syslog server rows, disable and re-enable log syslogd (or the equivalent in the GUI); until then the box sends nothing and the card shows no sender.

Out of scope, and stated so in the manual: SNMPv3 (no User Security Model yet; it arrives when a customer needs it), SNMP traps (SATOM sends none and receives none), flow telemetry (NetFlow, sFlow) and packet capture.

Target fields#

Field Description Required Example
Interval (min) Minimum minutes between two runs of this target; clamped to 1–1440 Yes 3
top Number of busiest policies read (only traffic, transactions); 1–200 When shown 10
Enabled Whether the sweep runs this target Yes on

Example#

🧪Example — Halve the load of throughput sampling on a large FortiWeb

fweb-01 has 600 policies and its traffic target takes several seconds. Set its Interval (min) to 30 and top to 5, then save. The device total is still collected every run; only the five busiest policies get per-policy throughput.

Result#

  • Saving a target writes an audit entry metrics_target_update with the changes (interval=…, enabled/disabled, top_n=…).
  • Taking a snapshot writes metrics_snapshot; deleting one writes metrics_snapshot_delete.
  • Each run writes its series to the store and updates the row's last run, status, detail, series and ms.
  • Every run, successful or not, also writes satom_scrape_up for that target (1 = ok, 0 = failed), so a broken collector is visible in the store. The built-in Collectors failing panels on Analytics chart exactly this.

Troubleshooting#

Store status shows "DOWN"#

Possible causes - The satom-metrics service is stopped, or the binary was not installed. - The configured store URL is wrong.

Solution 1. On the node, check systemctl status satom-metrics. 2. Run satom diagnose all; it reports the metrics store binary and service. 3. Start or reinstall the service.

Verification — the badge shows up and a series count.

A target shows "error"#

Hover the badge or read the detail under it — it carries the device's error (timeout, authentication, refused). The sweep itself still counts as having run. Fix the device access (see Appliances) and wait for the next run or click Run sweep now.

"N device(s) with no collection"#

Each device is listed with a reason:

Reason Meaning
no collectors exist for <kind> yet the product has no collector
device is in maintenance maintenance suppresses collection entirely
retired — host neutralised the host ends in .invalid
no host configured the appliance has no host
not provisioned yet — runs on the next sweep targets are created on the next sweep

"No targets yet"#

Targets are created when an appliance is saved and again on every sweep. Click Run sweep now or wait for metrics_scrape.

"Peer dual-write … consecutive failure(s)"#

Shown after Run sweep now when the optional HA mirror is on and failing; the Peer dual-write line on the store card shows the same state, the last success and the consecutive failures. Local collection is unaffected. See Advanced.

Collection is slower than the interval I set#

A target only runs when the metrics_scrape sweep ticks and its interval has elapsed (with 45 seconds of tolerance). With a 3-minute sweep, choose intervals that are multiples of 3.

Advanced#

Advanced The store
  • Runs as satom-metrics.service: victoria-metrics listening on 127.0.0.1:8428 only, data in /var/lib/satom-metrics, -retentionPeriod=396d, memory capped at 512 MiB, query duration capped at 30 s.
  • Reads and writes have no authentication; the loopback bind is their protection. All queries go through SATOM (session + ADOM scoping). Do not rebind it.
  • Its administrative endpoints (series deletion, snapshots, force-merge, reload, flags, profiling and similar) require keys. install-metrics-store.sh generates them once into the root-only /etc/satom/metrics-auth.env, which the service reads at start, so the keys appear neither in the unit file nor on the command line. The application holds only the snapshot key it needs for Take snapshot and Delete, in /etc/satom/metrics-snapshot.key (readable by the service account); it never sends that key off the node.
  • It lives outside SATOM's data/ directory and is not part of system backups. Each HA node has its own store; losing it loses graphs, not configuration.
  • The store URL can be overridden by the metrics.vm_url setting or an environment variable (container installs).
Advanced Sweep mechanics
  • The sweep first auto-creates missing targets for every appliance (insert-only — your edits are never overwritten), then runs due targets in parallel, at most 8 at a time.
  • Devices in maintenance and retired hosts (*.invalid) get no targets and are skipped.
  • The sweep reports success even when devices fail; per-target status carries the failures.
Advanced Optional peer dual-write (HA)

When the setting metrics.peer_dual_write is on, every scrape is also mirrored to the other HA node's store over the authenticated inter-node channel (HTTPS 8443 to a verified peer certificate, each request HMAC-signed with the node identity key), so a promoted standby keeps history. The peer address comes from metrics.peer_host or the HA node registry. It is off by default, and in this release there is no field for it on any settings page. A failing mirror never fails the local scrape; its state (off, unconfigured, unavailable, pending, unreachable, rejected, ok) is journalled in /opt/satom/state/metrics-peer.json, shown on the Peer dual-write line of the Collection page and reported after Run sweep now. The receiving endpoints refuse writes (503) when no node identity key is configured.

Advanced Store snapshots

The Take snapshot button posts to /monitoring/collection/snapshot (config_write), which takes a hot (hard-link) snapshot of the local store and records metrics_snapshot; a delete through the same endpoint records metrics_snapshot_delete. The card reads GET /monitoring/collection/snapshots (local store) and GET /monitoring/collection/stores (every node, including the peer) after the page has loaded, so a slow store or peer never delays the page. Snapshots never expire on their own.
